title: Nick Nurse smartly responds to Kevin Durant’s viral 76ers-Warriors comparison
description: Philadelphia 76ers head coach Nick Nurse responds to Kevin Durant’s take on the team. The 2026-27 NBA season is yet to begin, but Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant has already hailed the Philadelphia 76ers as the team to beat.
fullText:
Philadelphia 76ers head coach Nick Nurse responds to Kevin Durant's take on the team.

The 2026-27 NBA season is yet to begin, but Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant has already hailed the Philadelphia 76ers as the team to beat.

Additionally, KD compared the current 76ers roster to the iconic 2016-17 Golden State Warriors team and asked the fans to treat them similarly. After all, the 2016-17 Warriors were considered unfair.

Since KD's comments, Draymond Green and Klay Thompson have been very vocal, and now 76ers head coach Nick Nurse has joined the conversation.

Nurse essentially downplayed the comparison during an interview with NBC Sports Philadelphia.

"Championship teams have a lot of similar characteristics," Nurse said. "And the first thing is, is we need to get to work, right? I really still put hard work and work ethic and all that stuff at the top of the list if you want to win."

He added, "Are we going to outwork our opponents, right? Are we going to watch better film, more film, spend more hours?"

In a way, Nurse agreed with Durant, but also pointed out that no matter how talented a roster is, it won't win the NBA Championship without an elite work ethic.

title: Voice-cloned video falsely claims NBA coach planned to recruit late Filipino basketball player
description: T he death of young Filipino basketball player Rene Baterbonia at a training camp in June captivated social media users in the Philippines, including a TikTok post falsely claiming that an NBA coach had planned to recruit the 18-year-old for the 2026-27 season. AFP found that the clip had been digitally altered, while the original video was published before Baterbonia's death.
fullText:
T he death of young Filipino basketball player Rene Baterbonia at a training camp in June captivated social media users in the Philippines, including a TikTok post falsely claiming that an NBA coach had planned to recruit the 18-year-old for the 2026-27 season. AFP found that the clip had been digitally altered, while the original video was published before Baterbonia's death.

"OKC Thunder coach planned to recruit Rene Baterbonia after seeing his potential during his basketball games," the overlaid Tagalog-language text on a TikTok clip reads.

The post has racked up over 869,000 views since it was published on July 20. It claims Baterbonia "would've been the first pure Filipino to join the NBA".

The TikTok video shows Mark Daigneault, head coach of the NBA's Oklahoma City Thunder (OKC Thunder), speaking at a press conference ( archived link).

Daigneault can be heard saying they planned to draft Baterbonia, an 18-year-old college student at Ateneo De Manila University, before he died (archived here and here).

"Over the past year, our scouts closely followed Rene Baterbonia and were impressed by his talent, work ethic, and potential," he appears to say in the clip.

"Internally, we were preparing to select him in the 2026 to 2027 NBA draft and had even discussed a multi-year contract worth approximately 25 million US dollars."

"Unfortunately, events took an unexpected turn, and those plans will never become real."

Social media users shared the same clip on TikTok and Facebook, after Baterbonia and teammate Divine Adili drowned during a team-building exercise in the eastern Philippines on June 8 ( archived link).

Their deaths and the subsequent investigation by authorities unleashed a frenzy of social media posts about Baterbonia, a promising small-town athlete recently recruited into collegiate basketball.

Officials from his hometown of Talacogon in Mindanao island released a statement on July 30, asking the public to stop soliciting financial assistance for the Baterbonia family and to stop posting visits to the basketball player's grave for content ( archived link).

But this video has been altered and the original YouTube video was published on May 31, eight days before Baterbonia's death.

A reverse image search using the clip's keyframes found the original unedited version of the video published on the OKC Thunder's official YouTube channel ( archived link).

The video's description reads: "Head Coach Mark Daigneault speaks with the media at end-of-season interviews."

Daigneault made no mention of Baterbonia in the entirety of the video.

A close inspection of the altered footage found that Daigneault's mouth did not match the audio.

Using the Hiya detection tool within the Verification Plugin found the clip's audio was "very likely AI-generated".

title: In financial move, Rockets release JD Davison from non-guaranteed deal
description: To officially dip below the NBA’s 2026-27 luxury tax line, the Houston Rockets released backup guard JD Davison. He was on a non-guaranteed contract.
fullText:
In a move designed to clear space beneath the NBA's 2026-27 luxury tax, the Rockets announced the release of backup guard JD Davison on Wednesday.

Davison's minimum contract for next season was not yet guaranteed, and the 23-year-old does not have any remaining two-way eligibility. He played most of 2025-26 on a two-way deal.

As things stand, Davison's path to a standard roster spot had become much more difficult after Houston's offseason acquisitions of Bruce Thornton and Marcus Smart, a pair of guards who played last season with Ohio State and the Los Angeles Lakers.

Davison's release does open up an additional training camp roster spot, which could be used to evaluate a non-guaranteed player who is either eligible for a two-way contract or potentially a fit for Houston's G League affiliate, the Rio Grande Valley (RGV) Vipers.

NBA teams are allowed to carry up to 21 players in the offseason and into the preseason, but that number dips to a maximum of 15 standard deals and three two-way slots for the regular season, which begins in late October.

This leaves the Rockets $14,077 under the luxury tax with 14 players.

That amount is worth one day of service for the veteran minimum.

If they don’t make any additional moves this season, they could sign a 15th player on the last day of the season and finish with $0 tax space. https://t.co/CeAZXgxUdt

As for Davison, a former G League Most Valuable Player (MVP), the 6-foot-1 guard has proven all there is to prove at that level. Thus, he's likely to seek out another NBA opportunity elsewhere.

In 28 games with the Rockets last season, Davison averaged 2.5 points in 7.8 minutes, and he was a dependable ball-handler and perimeter defender, as well.

A waiver of Davison was long considered an inevitability, especially after the Rockets drafted Bruce Thornton. It's also the answer to a very simple math problem.

title: NBA Europe will take UK to another level - Anunoby
description: The planned launch of a bespoke European NBA league has the potential to take basketball in the United Kingdom to the "next level", says the New York Knicks' OG Anunoby.
fullText:
The planned launch of a bespoke European NBA league has the potential to take basketball in the United Kingdom to the "next level", says the New York Knicks' OG Anunoby.

With the working title of NBA Europe, it is planned for launch in October 2027 and is aiming to have 16 European teams - with London and Manchester expected to be included.

The deadline for final bids to own franchises was in June and it is hoped the identities of teams that will feature will begin to be announced this year, with the NBA receiving bids between $500m (£372m) and $1bn (£745m) for each target host city.

Anunoby is the standout current player of UK origin in the NBA, having played a starring role in the Knicks' first NBA title win since 1973.

Alongside the Portland Trail Blazers' Jeremy Sochan, the Boston Celtics' Amari Williams and Tobi Lawal, who is set to make his NBA debut this season for the Dallas Mavericks, Anunoby makes up part of the NBA's UK quartet.

"I think it is amazing," Anunoby told BBC Sport when asked about the NBA Europe plans.

"Basketball continues to grow, especially here in London and in Manchester.

"It's exciting and I think it is going to take basketball to another level out here."

Plans for the league's launch in just over a year's time remain "on track", with the league set to start in tandem with the 2027-28 NBA season.

"Planning is going really well. We've had an amazing amount of demand in the last couple of months for NBA Europe, particularly as bidding closed," said Laura Pinnell, vice-president and head of Consumer Group for the NBA across Europe and the Middle East.

"I would say the UK is one of the biggest opportunities for us out of the whole project.

"The growth opportunity is incredible and actually a London franchise, there is discussion about a Manchester franchise. All of which are great opportunities for fans and also, youth and participation."

Anunoby, a two-time NBA Championship winner, has spent time in his birth city of London this week during his off-season break.

As well as investing his own money as part of a grassroots court development in Camden, Anunoby has been eyeing the prospect of helping the Knicks win a second NBA title in as many years next season.

The NBA has had eight different champions in as many years, with no team being able to produce back-to-back titles since the Golden State Warriors in 2017 and 2018.

"That's our goal this year," said Anunoby in response to the prospect of ending the run of consecutive different winners.

But asked which of the Knicks' 29 NBA rivals will pose their biggest threat, the 29-year-old said challenges will come from across the competition.

"The whole league," added Anunoby.

"It is a very tough league and every team is capable and everyone is a threat."

title: LeBron James Philadelphia 76ers Tribute Goes Viral
description: Philadelphia is already embracing LeBron James, with a new Sixers mural of the four-time NBA champion attracting attention in Fairmount. The post LeBron James Philadelphia 76ers Tribute Goes Viral appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Philadelphia muralist Bill Strobel appears to be behind the LeBron James tribute attracting attention in the city’s Fairmount section.

The completed artwork depicts James in a black Philadelphia 76ers No. 23 jersey against a red-and-blue background. Its signature, @billstro4_art, matches Strobel’s Instagram handle.

A close-up of the completed mural shows the handle @billstro4_art painted beside the image. That account belongs to Bill Strobel, a Philadelphia artist with an established connection to the city’s sports murals.

Strobel previously painted a Jalen Hurts mural in Fairmount before the Philadelphia Eagles’ Super Bowl appearance. The Eagles described that project as one Strobel initiated himself at Brown and Corinthian Streets. He has also produced artwork for Lincoln Financial Field and other prominent Philadelphia locations.

The attribution turns the Sixers mural into more than an anonymous viral tribute. It appears to be the latest work from an artist who has repeatedly used Philadelphia’s walls to mark significant moments involving the city’s teams.

The mural appeared less than a week after the Sixers officially announced that James would wear No. 23 in Philadelphia.

James, 41, joined the Sixers after eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers. He described the move as the final major decision of his playing career and said the opportunity to compete for another championship helped lead him to Philadelphia.

That context makes the mural more than an imaginative picture of James in another team’s uniform. He is now actually a member of the Sixers, joining a roster built around Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe.

Philadelphia has not won an NBA championship since 1983. James, meanwhile, has won four titles across three franchises. Another championship would make him the first player to win one with four different NBA teams.

The finished mural presents James in a familiar pose, wearing his trademark No. 23 with “Sixers” across his chest. Its appearance in Fairmount reflects the speed with which his signing has moved from transaction news to something Philadelphia fans can see in their own neighborhood.

James wearing a Philadelphia uniform once existed only in mock-ups and recruiting pitches.

The Sixers pursued him during the summer of 2018, when a Philadelphia contingent met with his representative, Rich Paul. James ultimately signed with the Lakers, beginning an eight-year run in Los Angeles instead.

Philadelphia’s interest was especially visible that year because billboards attempted to recruit James to the Sixers. Eight years later, he finally chose the franchise, turning those old hypothetical images into reality.

That history gives the Fairmount artwork an added layer. It is not a fan campaign trying to convince James to come to Philadelphia. It is a celebration of a move that has already happened.

James’ signing immediately raised the Sixers’ expectations, although their championship prospects will depend heavily on health, chemistry and how their collection of high-usage stars fits together. The mural captures the more optimistic side of the moment: Philadelphia has a new superstar, and the city is already making space for him.

LeBron is one of the greatest basketball players of all time, but he also might be one of the best basketball businessmen ever, with both titles being contested with Michael Jordan.

James has a reported net worth of $1.4 billion according to Forbes, but he has two pieces of prized memorabilia that don’t factor into that worth.

James was doing an interview with Topps where they discussed the rarest cards to have sold with his likeness on it, with James revealing he might have his own $5.2 million rookie edition card in a vault.

“I think my rookie card sold for the most, but I heard it’s like crazy. I happen to maybe have one or two of those cards locked in a vault somewhere. So, just in case I ever fall on hard times, I’m good.”

James joked about how those rookie cards will help him get back on his feet if he ever falls on hard times, but he has more than enough levers to pull.

Most of his game-worn memorabilia from major highlights of his career could be more valuable than a rookie Topps card, but if you put it all together, James could add $100 million to his net worth just by putting an actual value on these items.

James’ $5.2 million 2003 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Rookie Patch Autograph card actually cost $6.4 million to the new owner after all fees and taxes were accounted for.

If James were to sell his own personal version of the card, it’d be far more valuable because it is a verifiable belonging of James, not just a card that came out of a pack.

The most expensive sports card of all time cost $12.9 million in August 2025, a 2007–08 Upper Deck Exquisite Collection Dual Logoman Autograph with both Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant.

Cards with LeBron as a rookie are bound to become more valuable in the coming years, especially after he retires from the sport.

The billionaire James can afford to play on minimum NBA contracts in his twilight due to his shrewd off-court success, so it’s unlikely he’d suddenly lose his fortune and need to sell cards and memorabilia to restart his life.

While the NBA world is still bumping with emotion over the LeBron James to Philadelphia 76ers news, the Cleveland Cavaliers are still processing what hit them.

Not only did James say no to a storybook reunion, but he joined the conference rival instead. So what led to the four-time league MVP passing on a reunion when many were convinced that was his best path forward?

According to NBA insider Brett Siegel, the Cavs decision to not trade for Jaylen Brown likely played a major role in James saying no to Cleveland.

“The issue of the Cavaliers not making any moves to improve their roster, specifically not pursuing Jaylen Brown when Boston was making him available, also clearly influenced James’ decision. If Cleveland was willing to part ways with Evan Mobley in a deal for Brown, that would’ve weighed heavily in LeBron’s mind, but this is simply a hypothetical game at this juncture.”

LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – FEBRUARY 22: Jaylen Brown #7 of the Boston Celtics attempts a shot against LeBron James #23 of the Los Angeles Lakers during the first half of their game at Crypto.com Arena on February 22, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luiza Moraes/Getty Images)

The Cavs thought they were sitting pretty by not making any moves. They wanted to preserve all the flexibility needed to add James to the roster and, perhaps, pay him significantly more than what competing teams could offer.

Instead, they may have been watching their chances to land The King quickly fade away as James held back to see which teams were making big moves.

The Sixers pulled the trigger. They landed Brown, the 29-year-old perennial All-Star, from the Boston Celtics in a stunning, and rather lopsided, trade.

Clearly, that move caught James’ eyes and ears. According to ESPN’s Shams Charania, the Sixers did not register on James’ radar until they acquired Brown.

“Philadelphia, I’m telling you was not even on this radar, was not in the pool of candidates until Bob Myers went out and got Jaylen Brown that changed the equation,” Charania said on ESPN’s First Take Friday morning following James’ move to the Sixers. “The Sixers got on the map and from there it became for LeBron James now almost four weeks of deliberation with LeBron James, Rich Paul, that inner circle there and his family, eventually.”

HOUSTON, TEXAS – MARCH 16: LeBron James #23 of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the National Anthem prior to the game against the Houston Rockets at Toyota Center on March 16, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images)

The day after the James news was announced, ESPN’s Brian Windhorst laid out the three biggest reasons why James chose Philadelphia over Cleveland.

“In the end, there were three strikes against Cleveland: Family not being an issue in LeBron’s choice, the front office not making a deal for (Jaylen) Brown and the Cavs’ roster not featuring (Darius) Garland. To say it was one of these factors more than the other might be missing the big picture,” Windhorst wrote.

Garland, James’ fellow Klutch Sports client, was moved to the Los Angeles Clippers for James Harden in a trade in February. Windhorst believes the Cavs’ decision to move Garland, with whom James has a strong relationship, is another reason why James didn’t return to Cleveland.

If that is also true, then it boils down to this: the Cavs lost James months before he ever signed with the 76ers. The Garland trade in February started the slide, and not making a move for Brown this summer became the final blow.

title: Brandon Jennings Is Right: Jayson Tatum Took a Shot at Jaylen Brown
description: Jaylen Brown remained at the center of NBA conversation after the Boston Celtics sent him to the Philadelphia 76ers in a trade built around Paul George. Criticism of Boston’s return soon created a more personal question: Did the Celtics decide they could no longer manage Brown’s personality?Jayson Tatum then delivered a leadership lesson at an […] The post Brandon Jennings Is Right: Jayson Tatum Took a Shot at Jaylen Brown appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Jaylen Brown remained at the center of NBA conversation after the Boston Celtics sent him to the Philadelphia 76ers in a trade built around Paul George. Criticism of Boston’s return soon created a more personal question: Did the Celtics decide they could no longer manage Brown’s personality?

Jayson Tatum then delivered a leadership lesson at an event for The Jayson Tatum Foundation that sounded remarkably connected to the debate surrounding his former teammate, Yahoo reports.

“Being around somebody that feels like they know it all, I don’t wanna be around that person,” Tatum said. “I don’t wanna be the smartest person in the room, I want to learn from somebody else.”

Brandon Jennings did not accept that statement as generic guidance for young players. After reposting the clip on X, Jennings wrote, “Motivational message my a-s lmaooo that’s a shot at Jaylen Brown.”

Tatum never mentioned Brown, leaving room for another explanation. Still, Jennings’ conclusion fits the timing and familiar language too well to dismiss.

Motivational message my ass lmaooo that’s a shot at Jaylen Brown https://t.co/y7m1mcZpuW

— Brandon Jennings (@Tuff__Crowd) July 25, 2026

Fox Sports host Colin Cowherd previously said two NBA sources characterized Brown as a difficult locker room presence because of how highly he regards his own intelligence.

“He suddenly thinks he’s the smartest guy in every room he’s in,” Cowherd said. “You get into a really bad place.”

Brown rejected Cowherd’s premise during a livestream after the trade, USA Today reports. The 29-year-old argued that intelligence takes different forms and said he never viewed himself as the smartest person present. He then questioned the intellectual standard across the sports business.

“No offense to everybody in sports, but the bar is fu—– low,” Brown said. “You know what I mean. The bar isn’t that high.”

Brown aimed that criticism broadly, not specifically at Tatum. However, Tatum’s choice to warn against someone who “feels like they know it all,” then invoke the same smartest-person framing, made the comparison unavoidable.

Could Brown’s comment have irritated Tatum? No public statement proves it. Their separation still changes the dynamic. Brown no longer needs to smooth over every ambiguous remark for Boston’s locker room, and Tatum does not have to seek reassurance from a teammate who now plays for a conference rival.

Without that clarification, Tatum can interpret Brown’s words however he wants. Jennings merely said aloud what many viewers heard beneath the motivational packaging.

The basketball backdrop gives this exchange more weight. Tatum’s Achilles rehabilitation limited him to 16 regular-season appearances after the injury he sustained during the 2024-25 playoffs. He returned late and participated in Boston’s postseason run, apart from Game 7 against Philadelphia.

Brown carried a leading role during Tatum’s absence. Across 71 games, he set career highs with 28.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists per contest. Brown also made the All-Star team, earned Second Team All-NBA recognition and ranked No. 6 in the MVP race.

That individual success did not produce Boston’s desired ending. The Celtics surrendered a 3-1 advantage against the 76ers, the team Brown later joined, and the collapse intensified scrutiny of his leadership as a primary option.

Tatum’s remarks do not confirm that he blamed Brown for Boston’s problems. They do, however, sound like a pointed response to the criticism that followed Brown out of Boston. Of every way Tatum could have discussed leadership, he selected language already attached to the loudest conversation about his former co-star.

That is why Jennings is right about the subtext. Until Tatum offers a different explanation, every Celtics-76ers meeting will invite another look at whether their long-running partnership ended with more friction than either star has acknowledged.

title: ‘YOU JOINED THE EAST FAVORITES!’ – Skip Bayless Accuses LeBron James of ‘Ring Chasing’ After 76ers Move

fullText:
Skip Bayless joined the NBA world in reacting to LeBron James’ decision on Friday to join the Philadelphia 76ers. The talk show host, a known and unapologetic critic of the former Los Angeles Lakers superstar, wasted little time in sharing his thoughts about James signing a two-year, $8 million deal to play in Philly.

As usual, Bayless didn’t hold back after James ended his three-week hold-up in free agency by going to a team loaded with talent.

The 76ers were reportedly not on James’ radar until they acquired Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics. Without giving up VJ Edgecombe or Tyrese Maxey, Philadelphia now has a stacked core that is as good, if not better, than any NBA team.

After nearly a month of speculation, the 22-time All-Star snubbed the Miami Heat, Golden State Warriors, Minnesota Timberwolves, and Cleveland Cavaliers, the other frontrunners to get his signature.

A few hours after news broke that James is now a 76er, Bayless reacted.

“CONGRATS, LEBRON! YOU MADE THE OBVIOUS RING-CHASING CHOICE! YOU JOINED THE EAST FAVORITES!” Bayless tweeted.

On Friday’s “The Skip Bayless Show,” the veteran sports journalist added more context to his message.

“This wasn’t about basketball happiness! … This was about ring chasing. What team gave LeBron James the best chance to win a fifth, maybe even a sixth championship? It was obviously from the start the Philadelphia 76ers,” Bayless said.

According to Bayless, the 41-year-old superstar wouldn’t take his talents to the Golden State Warriors, which the podcaster named the “Olden State,” if James had gone there.

Bayless continued that he didn’t predict the Timberwolves to win the James sweepstakes, as the 21-time All-NBA wouldn’t want to live in Minneapolis.

The Cavaliers offered a storybook ending, but Bayless didn’t see this version of James as the right fit on that roster.

For the former Fox Sports talk show host, the “happiness” driven decision for James would have been to take his talents back to South Beach, where he could compete for a championship and play golf “all year round.”

The allure of returning to a place where he won two championships and where Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo now lead the roster was not enough to sway James.

MORE: ‘Legacy-Wise, It Didn’t Add Up’ – LeBron James’ Former Teammate Questions NBA Legend’s $8 Million 76ers Deal

Bayless said that it was a no-brainer for James to choose Philadelphia after the 76ers pulled off what he called the “steal of the century” by getting Brown.

The analyst also argued that Maxey and VJ Edgecombe provide enviable youth and speed to surround a player entering his 24th NBA season.

Finally, there is Joel Embiid, who, when healthy, Bayless called the closest the NBA has seen to a Shaquille O’Neal.

Bayless’ criticism of James isn’t new or surprising. Over the past few years, he has been taking shots at the Akron, Ohio, native’s championships, claiming they were won by stacking his teams.

James likely knew he would be criticized regardless of which team he chose to play for. Bayless took his shots, but the only thing that matters to the 76ers’ brand-new acquisition is a chance to win championship No. 5.

title: NBA best & worst offseason moves now that LeBron is in Philly
description: The best and the worst moves of the offseason.
fullText:

title: NBA superstar LeBron James to join Philadelphia 76ers
description: Basketball superstar LeBron James announces he will join the Philadelphia 76ers for what he says will be his final contract in the NBA.
fullText:
LeBron James has announced he will be joining the Philadelphia 76ers next season for what he says will be his final contract in the NBA.

The 41-year-old, the highest points scorer in the history of the league, left the Los Angeles Lakers after eight years last month.

The Cleveland Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors, Minnesota Timberwolves and Miami Heat were also rumoured to be in the running for the four-time NBA champion.

"I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energise a new fanbase and start this incredible journey one last time," James said on X.

James has won an NBA title with all three teams he previously played for. He won two with Miami, who earlier this week mistakenly posted a link to an 'introductory press conference' for James.

A Heat spokesperson told Reuters the video was posted in error by staff who were preparing for the possibility of James rejoining the team he played for between 2010 and 2014.

Either side of that Miami stint, James had two spells with Cleveland, who drafted James in 2003 and are based near his hometown of Akron, Ohio.

"Miami I'll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always [be] home," James added.

James helped the Cavs become NBA champions in 2016 and joined the Lakers in 2018, claiming another NBA title two years later.

He has been named the NBA's Most Valuable Player four times, all between 2009 and 2013, and has been an NBA All-Star the last 22 seasons running.

'Maybe he's a racist' - Trump critical of James

James said after last season that he was "pretty sure I [had] played my last game" but realised "I still truly love this game and I have more to give".

ESPN has reported that James has signed a two-year contract, with a player option for the second year, worth $8m (£6m). His average salary with the Lakers last season was $50.7m (£38m).

James added: "I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point?

"I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship."

The 76ers reached the Conference semi-finals in last season's play-offs, where they lost to the eventual champions, the New York Knicks.

They have since acquired Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics, in exchange for Paul George and some future draft picks.

title: NBA Trade Rumors: After LeBron James Decision, Massive Moves Ahead
description: NBA trade rumors are back in swing now that the league has gotten LeBron James' decision. He is heading to Philadelphia ... and now what? The post NBA Trade Rumors: After LeBron James Decision, Massive Moves Ahead appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Well that’s that. LeBron James has shocked the NBA and made a remarkable choice, opting to play for the Sixers for the next two years in a move that will have massive reverberations around the league. And we’re now ready to kick the old NBA trade rumor mill back into gear.

So what is coming next? We asked, let’s look …

James Harden. There was some question as to whether the Cavaliers would work as a unit if both Harden and James were on the team alongside Donovan Mitchell. Now, that won’t be an issue. But the Cavaliers now will have to finish up their summer with a contract for Harden and some sort of way to fill out the roster–they can add at least one more player, and they’ve been linked to DeMar DeRozan, Mario Hezonja and Jonathan Kuminga. Of note: The Cavs do want to give significant minutes to young players Meleek Thomas and Jaylon Tyson this season.

Draymond Green. The Warriors were holding off on signing Green in hopes of adding James. Now that James is off the board, the Warriors will give Green their remaining cap room but will still be on the lookout for another addition–they’re in the market for DeRozan and Hezonja. There’s an outside chance that the Warriors could move Moses Moody in a deal, and may have interest in Cam Johnson.

Peyton Watson. The Nuggets are still holding out hope to keep Watson in restricted free agency. Now that the James situation is settled, the Nuggets could finally seek to trade away Cam Johnson, who has not been the target that many expected thus far. The Nuggets have rebuffed interest in Johnson so far, but that could change.

Mario Hezonja. Hezonja has made his return to the NBA a notable one, as he has been one of the best players in the Spanish league after flaming out during three stops in the league after he’d been the No. 5 overall pick. Can Hezonja still play? That’s unclear but he’s done well to hype himself up as a contributor for contenders who are now bidding on his services.

Jonathan Kuminga. This has been the big donut in the coffee of the NBA offseason, and Kuminga remains the subject of sign-and-trade rumors. But the Hawks do not want players back, and will want some draft compensation no matter what. Can they get anyone to pay it? The Cavs are a longshot, as are the Lakers, and there are expected to be others in the mix.

DeMar DeRozan. He was waived by the Kings, and it is unlikely he will follow James to the Sixers. Miami? Cleveland? Warriors? His options are open.

Bradley Beal. The Miami Heat? That makes the most sense for Beal, who has been linked to the Celtics, Cavaliers, Warriors and others.

Bronny James. Will he join his father in Philadelphia? Many think he should stay in Los Angeles, including some with the Lakers who have liked his development. It should be time to sink or swim in the NBA for Bronny James, but if his dad wants him in Philly, that’s where he will go.

Well, no one expected Anthony Davis and Kyrie Irving to pop back up on the NBA market here in late July but, the rumor mill is never-ending. Neither is expected to get moved, but they’re still being talked about  …

Anthony Davis, Wizards. (Remaining contract: two years, $121 million, including player option.) Davis has been the subject of much speculation this offseason, but around the league, there isn’t a sense he is going to be dealt. The Wizards would like to get Davis on the floor and see if he can help them compete for a playoff spot. If not, he could be dealt by the February trade deadline.

Zion Williamson, Pelicans. (Remaining contract: two years, $87 million.) We’re not expecting Williamson to be moved by the end of the summer, but if he stays on the floor early in the year, New Orleans has plenty of incentive to find a new spot for him. A frontcourt of Derik Queen and Williamson makes little sense.

Kevin Durant, Rockets. (Remaining contract: two years, $90 million, player option.) There does not seem to be a market for Durant, who is 37 and has $90 million over two years on his contract. Rumors of Pistons interest has faded as the focus there is on re-signing Jalen Duren. Maybe a Durant deal comes back up after that gets done? It’s a longshot.

Jamal Murray, Nuggets. (Remaining contract: three years, $160 million.) The Nuggets are on track to operate over the second apron, which is not a place any team–especially a Kroenke team–likes to operate. Dealing Murray could shave some money off the cap but he was an All-Star last year and dumping him might be too much to ask of the Nuggets.

Jimmy Butler, Warriors. (Remaining contract: one year, $57 million.) It just does not appear that the Warriors are looking to move Butler. He’s the team’s main path to adding another star, as he is probably out until Christmas or later as he recovers from January ACL surgery. There are not many teams looking to add a rehabbing 36-year-old to their mix, and the Warriors are not likely to find a player who is better than Butler when healthy.

It’s hard to bring in a young star–or even a young potential star–on the trade market. But there could be some wrangling for these guys, the 25-and-under (OK, 26 for Trey Murphy) crowd.

Moses Moody, Warriors. (Remaining contract: two years, $26 million.) Moody him self said he is “curious” about what will happen to him on the trade market. Will James’ decision change that? He has developed into a valuable piece for Golden State, but a nasty knee injury could keep him out for most of next season.

Jalen Duren, Pistons. (Remaining contract: restricted free agent.) Sign-and-trade options for Duren are all but extinguished–were the Pistons ever really weighing a deal with the Kings for Domantas Sabonis? The Pistons have made moves to be able to give Duren more money, and that’s the likely way this all plays out.

Trey Murphy, Pelicans. (Remaining contract: three years, $88 million.) Murphy is a favorite in NBA trade rumors, but there are questions on how serious New Orleans would be about trading him. One exec says it will take a Desmond Bane-style offer (four first-round picks) to pry him from New Orleans, though that price has dropped a bit. Still, there’s been no movement yet.

Peyton Watson, Nuggets. (Remaining contract: restricted free agent.) The long restricted free-agent slog is on for Watson, and the Nuggets have surprised many by not being aggressive in moving players to create some breathing room to keep Watson. The sign-and-trade market reportedly includes the Clippers, Hawks and Bucks, but there is not much yet that would attract the Nuggets’ attention on a deal.

Nikola Jovic, Heat. (Remaining contract: four years, $62 million.) There is trepidation about trading for Jovic, who is certainly available and is still only 23 years old. But the remaining contract is a hefty bite for teams to take.

LeBron James will create an NBA trade rumor ripple effect, and the East could feel it most.

Michael Porter Jr., Nets. (Remaining contract: one year, $40 million, partial guarantee.) Porter is in the final year of his deal and wants an extension that starts at about what he is making now. The Nets likely won’t go that high, and if no middle ground is found, we are in for another heap of trade talk. Even if Porter is extended, he could be a trade candidate by next February’s deadline.

Grant Williams, Hornets. (Remaining contract: one year, $15 million.) The Hornets are not quite done with their roster, and Williams’ expiring deal has some value. He can still be a worthy big man off the bench.

Royce O’Neale, Hornets. (Remaining contract: two years, $21 million,) The Hornets would not be able to trade O’Neale with anyone else yet, so they could wait on a deal. But the team has gotten calls about moving him on after he’s come over from the Suns.

Jarrett Allen, Cavaliers. (Remaining contract: three years, $90 million.) As with Mobley, if the Cavs entice LeBron James to Cleveland, Allen could be trade bait. It’s more likely that Allen gets traded than Mobley, and the Cavaliers could get some relief and a contributor. Allen is a standard offensive center but is a valued rim-runner who can protect the paint.

Max Strus, Cavaliers. (Remaining contract: one year, $16 million.) The Cavs are trying hard to fit everything under the second apron, and that likely means moving off Strus, if they can find a taker.

Dennis Schroder, Cavaliers. (Remaining contract: one year, $14.6 million.) Schroder has played for 11 teams in the NBA so far, and the Cavs would be open to making it 12 as they seek to duck the second apron and still stay in the contending picture.

Myles Turner, Bucks. (Remaining contract: three years, $80 million.) Two things may well both be true on Turner–the Bucks are not shopping him because they want some veterans on hand, and there is no interest in him from other teams because of his contract.

Kyle Kuzma, Bucks. (Remaining contract: one year, $20 million,) His expiring contract is attractive and if the Bucks pull a sign-and-trade for Peyton Watson, Bennedict Mathurin or Jonathan Kuminga, he figures to be involved.

Jake LaRavia, Lakers. (Remaining contract: one year, $6 million.) Hustles, plays every game, but inconsistent. His contract makes him an attractive piece, though.

Herb Jones, Pelicans. (Remaining contract: four years, $82 million, including player option.) Jones is a popular name on the market, but the Pelicans are said to want two first-round picks, and with Jones having struggled with injuries and his 3-point shot in the past two seasons, that’s probably too steep. His remaining contract scares off potential suitors, too.

Derrick Jones Jr., Clippers. (Remaining contract: one year, $10 million.) Jones is a defensive ace still, and his expiring contract gives the Clippers some wiggle room to move him. They’re caught in the Aspiration pause, however.

Rudy Gobert, Timberwolves. (Remaining contract: two years, $74 million, including player option.) The Wolves, according to a report in The Athletic, were offered Jaylen Brown with the Celtics wanting Rudy Gobert, plus picks, as part of a trade package. The Wolves turned that down, though there still has been interest in Gobert, who is up for an extension.

Keldon Johnson, Spurs. (Remaining contract: one year, $17.5 million.) The reigning Sixth Man of the Year is heading into the final season of his contract, and San Antonio is likely to phase out his minutes in favor of younger players. He is still a valued leader on the team, but he could be a chip worth cashing in if the Spurs can land a first-round pick.

Domantas Sabonis, Kings. (Remaining contract: two years, $93 million.) Sabonis has had some nibbles, but no bites. There was a rumor that the Hornets were planning to trade for him, but that proved fruitless. Then there was the Jalen Duren sign-and-trade with the Pistons, which was far-fetched from the beginning. This one might have to wait until the season gets going.

Jrue Holiday, Blazers. (Remaining contract: two years, $72 million, with player option.) Certainly, something has to give in Portland with the arrival of Morant. Holiday is not getting any younger, but he has value around the NBA.

Zach LaVine, Kings. (Remaining contract: one year, $49 million.) LaVine picked up the player option worth $49 million. There was some hope that he could be waived, but after the Kings let DeMar DeRozan go, they’ll keep LaVine on the books and hope they can find a place to dump him.

Aaron Gordon, Nuggets. (Remaining contract: three years, $110 million.) Gordon has struggled to stay healthy, but is still a valued connective piece when he plays. He needs to be a No. 3/4 option on a good team, and teams aren’t falling over themselves to cough up assets for that, and the Nuggets have not pushed hard for a trade.

Daniel Gafford, Mavericks. (Remaining contract: 3 years, $54 million.) Gafford will be 28 in October, and with the Mavs focused on getting younger, moving him along has been one of the team’s top options. The concern is whether the guy the Mavs want to be their stalwart center–Dereck Lively II–can stay healthy. Lively has played 98 games in three seasons.

PJ Washington, Mavericks. (Remaining contract: 4 years, $90 million.) Like Gafford, Washington is aging out of the Mavericks’ timeline, as he turns 28 this summer. He’s a stretch 4 who plays good defense, but his shooting has been suspect–he made just 32.5% of his 3s last year. Washington’s extension kicks in this year, though, so he might be a better trade target down the line.

Klay Thompson, Mavericks. (Remaining contract: one year, $17 million.) Another aging Mav! Thompson does not fit Dallas’s timeline, and if the Mavs can get anything–youth, a few second-rounders–for him, they will. He’s still a 38% 3-point shooter. The addition of Tarik Biberovic is more incentive to move Thompson.

Cam Johnson, Nuggets. (Remaining contract: one year, $23 million.) Johnson has been a disaster in Denver, and he has been a prominent feature on the NBA trade rumor mill for years now. He still has enough of a reputation around the league to warrant trade interest, but a report from The Stein Line suggests the Nuggets are not going that route … yet.

The NBA trade rumor mill has had a busy summer, interspersed with some controversy. Here are the top rumors that sprouted into actual trades …

Boston’s controversial decision to move Brown as he neared an extension on a supermax contract set off a round of second apron discussion in the NBA.

Celtics get: Paul George, a 2028 first-round pick that could convert to a swap, Philly’s 2031 unprotected first-rounder, and two second-round picks.

The deal that kicked off the summer was the one most expected to be expanded, but wound up staying a two-teamer. The Bucks are banking on this being enough for a rebuild, and the Heat were hoping this precedes a LeBron James return. Alas …

Bucks get: Tyler Herro, Kel’el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr. and Kasparas Jakucionis go to Milwaukee. Also Bucks got the 13th pick in the draft (Nate Ament) and future first-rounders, in 2031 and 2033, plus a future pick swap and a second-round pick.

Heat get: Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis.

The Wolves combined their two major transactions, taking a chance on bringing in LaMelo Ball and getting off the contract of Julius Randle.

Timberwolves get: LaMelo Ball, Josh Green, No. 33 pick (Isaiah Evans).

Hornets get: Naz Reid, Mouhamadou Gueye, rights to Matteo Spagnolo, Minnesota’s first-round pick in 2033, second round picks in 2029, 2032 and 2033, plus three swaps, also from Minnesota.

Nets get: Julius Randle, No. 28 pick (Joshua Jefferson).

Memphis finally moves on from Ja Morant, and was able to do so by taking on Jerami Grant’s contract–but did not have to include outgoing draft capital.

Grizzlies get: Jerami Grant and Kris Murray.

A classic NBA deal that started as Isaiah Stewart going to Memphis, but ballooned since.

Grizzlies get: Isaiah Stewart, D’Angelo Russell, AJ Johnson, five second-round picks. (Lose: Santi Aldama.)

Pistons get: John Collins, Taurean Prince, Gary Harris. (Lose: Isaiah Stewart, Caris LeVert, Marcus Sasser.)

Clippers get: Trade exception. (Lose: John Collins.)

Wizards get: Khris Middleton. (Lose: D’Angelo Russell.)

Bucks get: Caris LeVert. (Lose: Taurean Prince, Gary Harris, AJ Johnson.)

Mavericks get: Santi Aldama, Marcus Sasser. (Lose: Khris Middleton.)

Now,  this trade has been undone punishment for the Aspiration scandal has yet to be doled out, but it’s still likely to get done once that situation is settled. There are still a lot of questions about when that might be, though.

Clippers get: Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks (2031 and 2033), plus a swap and two second-round picks.

The Hornets had been looking for a taker for Bridges, whose past domestic violence charges scared off many teams. But Charlotte attached draft capital and the Suns took him in.

Suns get: Miles Bridges, 2029 first-round pick, 2027 second-round pick.

Hornets get: Grayson Allen, Royce O’Neale, 2033 first-round pick.

The Thunder jettisoned Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins for second-round picks early in July, and got all the way under the second apron by moving Lu Dort later in a three-team deal that saw former No. 1 overall pick Zaccharie Risacher dealt, too.

Hawks get: Lu Dort, Ryan Nembhard.

Thunder get: Three second-round picks.

Mavericks get: Zaccharie Risacher.

title: Where former Oregon PG Payton Pritchard lands in redo of 2020 NBA Draft
description: Payton Pritchard has far outperformed his No. 26 overall draft spot, but just how far does he rise in a 2020 NBA redraft?
fullText:
During Payton Pritchard's first four seasons in the NBA, he was largely used as an end-of-the-bench reserve for the Boston Celtics. As the 26th pick in the first round in the 2020 NBA Draft after four seasons with the Oregon Ducks, he had slightly begun to live up to the late-first-round billing in Year 4, averaging 9.6 points for a Celtics team that won the title.

But the rise continued into the 2024-25 season when point guard Jrue Holiday was traded away, clearing a prominent bench role for the former Duck. Pritchard averaged 14.3 points and 3.5 assists while converting on 40.7% of his triples, winning the NBA's Sixth Man of the Year award.

Now coming off a season in which he started 50 games for Boston and averaged a career-high 17.0 points and 5.2 assists, it's clear that Pritchard has far outpaced his 26th overall spot in the 2020 draft.

But just how far up would he go in a 2020 redraft?

According to The Ringer's Bill Simmons, Pritchard would go 10th overall, only behind stars such as Anthony Edwards, Tyrese Haliburton, Tyrese Maxey and several others.

"Pritchard took a couple years," Simmons said during an episode of The Bill Simmons Podcast. "I always liked him more than it seemed like the coaches liked him and it was always unclear why he wasn't getting the car keys a little bit more, and I think the team liked him because they gave him a contract even before he'd kind of become who he became. And then he just became one of the best bench guards in the league. Last year, he moved into a whole different level."

Heading into the 2026-27 season, Pritchard has a chance to move up yet another level. The Celtics traded away last years leading scorer Jaylen Brown, who took 21.7 shots per night. While Jayson Tatum and Paul George, who arrived via the Brown trade, will take some of those looks, the door is cracked open even more for an increased amount of Pritchard shots.

Already, Pritchard is making teams with picks in the 10's and early 20's of the 2020 draft wish they could've taken him, but that regret could reach an even higher mark in the seasons to come.

title: Why LeBron's new team — the 76ers! — should happily trade for Bronny James
description: If LeBron wants to continue playing with his son in the NBA, it should be a no-brainer for the 76ers.
fullText:
At long last, LeBron James has made his decision. The 41-year-old is a Sixer, signing a two-year deal worth $8 million to join Philadelphia.

For James' free agency, it's not clear what the exact terms of engagement were during this round. But unlike past courtships, the employment status of James' son Bronny will likely be part of internal discussions with LeBron's new team in Philly. In 2024, when James' Los Angeles Lakers selected Bronny with the 55th pick in the draft, the Jameses became the first father-son pairing to play in the NBA together.

LeBron has not publicly stated that he'd like his eldest son to join him, and it's not a given the Lakers would satisfy any such request. But it also wouldn't be a surprise to hear that LeBron would prefer to continue playing with his son. In the playoffs, after throwing an alley-oop to Bronny in a Game 3 win over the Houston Rockets, LeBron didn't hold back his joy.

"It just keeps getting better and better," he said after the game. "It's like, wow."

As of now, there is no plan or request for Bronny to join his father, per ESPN Ramona Shelburne. But that could always change as the season draws closer. Bronny for the time being remains on the Lakers' roster, set to play his third year on a four-year contract that he signed in 2024. The 21-year-old became a rotation player by the end of last season, garnering 16.9 minutes per game while appearing in eight playoff games with the Lakers.

But president Bob Myers and the Philadelphia 76ers should happily acquire Bronny. Here are three reasons why.

Is Bronny James a good NBA player? I don't think anyone would argue that he is right now. The better framework is to count him among the hundred or so players who are trying to make it in the league. In 556 minutes over two seasons, he's averaging 2.7 points, 1.1 assists and 0.6 rebounds. Not great. On a per-minute basis, his career PER of 8.4 is 464th among 485 players with at least 500 minutes over the last two seasons. Still: not great.

But he's trending upward. The swing skill for Bronny is his 3-point shot, which would allow him to level up his athleticism with a perimeter threat. Last season, he made 22 of his 57 3-point shots, giving him a promising 38.6% conversion rate, an improvement from his debut mark of 28.1%. If he can maintain a strong percentage and continue to deliver strong on-ball defense, he'll be able to carve out a role as an NBA player.

There's also G-League data. In his age-20 and age-21 seasons, his G-League ledger shows that there's something there. In 25 career games in the G-League, Bronny is averaging 18.4 points, 4.4 assists and 4.0 rebounds in 30 minutes per game while shooting 49.6% from the floor, 41.3% on six 3-pointers per game and 80.5% from the line. For a defensive-minded player like Bronny, scoring 22 points per 36 minutes with an above-average 63.9% true shooting percentage at the G-League suggests he's more than ready for NBA minutes.

Maybe Bronny doesn't pan out to be a Top 300 player one day. Gary Payton II bounced around the league before he found a real home in Golden State at age 29. Bronny is eight years younger than GP2 and, despite his youth, teams will have hundreds of millions of reasons to employ Bronny and his father.

He's already proven he's worthy of a roster spot. If you're annoyed by the nepotism at play, NBA history tells us that league executives have to pay off a debt to sons of NBA players who deserved better shots.

Do you remember Mladen Sekularac?

How about Cady Lalanne, Herbert Hill, Ejike Ugboaja, Rick Rickert, Maurice Jeffers, Kris Clack and Ronnie Henderson?

These names are among the 31 No. 55 selections since the draft expanded to that many picks in 1996. Which means that one out of every four No. 55s don't even make it to Game No. 1.

That's the thing about Bronny James. Players selected this late in the draft are basically blind dart throws, unlikely to make any impact in the league whatsoever.

Any Bronny analysis has to begin with the recognition of the longshot baseline, one that shows playing in a single game is already an accomplishment. Anything after that is cake. Consider this fact: in just two seasons, Bronny has already scored the 12th-most career points of the 31 selections at No. 55.

Lakers head coach JJ Redick gave Bronny his big opportunity at the end of last season, playing him real minutes as a fringe rotation player on a playoff team. That just doesn't usually happen for players drafted as late as he was, as young as he was. In fact, among the 144 players drafted since 2000 at the No. 55 slot or later, only 15 actually played by their age-21 season, or what amounts to about 10%, according to Stathead.com research tools. Bronny is getting minutes earlier than 90% of those who are drafted as late as he was. Through this lens, Bronny is ahead of the curve.

Did Bronny benefit from being LeBron James' son and get an earlier opportunity? Sure, but such a nepotistic benefit is long overdue considering that second-generation players have been snubbed more often than not in the past. The NBA draft tells the story that NBA progeny has been underrated.

In a span beginning with the modern two-round draft's debut in 1989 and 2022, there have been 62 players selected who were the sons of an NBA player. Some became future Hall of Famers, including Stephen Curry, Kobe Bryant and Jalen Brunson. Others became perennial All-Stars and champions, including Kevin Love, Al Horford and Klay Thompson.

As I pointed out last month advocating for Carlos Boozer's son, Cam, for the No. 1 pick, sons of NBA players are nearly twice as likely to become All-Stars than their non-legacy counterparts. The reality is that sons of NBA players like Bronny James have seemingly been punished, or at the very least overlooked, by teams for having a father who played in the league.

Despite their family's starpower, Scotty Pippen Jr., Gary Payton II and Seth Curry never heard their names called on draft night and have played a combined 26 seasons in the league. Even for second-generation players who don't have a box-office last name like Luke Kornet, Garrett Temple and Wesley Matthews, the fact that their fathers played in the NBA wasn't enough to get picked.

Punished might seem like too strong of a word, but the successes of undrafted sons of NBA players lends credence to the idea that GMs stiff the name-brand prospect, preferring instead to go for lesser-known diamonds in the rough that may make them look smarter for discovering. Like GP2 and Seth Curry, it took a while for some smaller second-gen players to carve out their NBA role. Considering that Bob Myers is playing with house money getting LeBron James at just the veteran minimum this season, trading for Bronny would be a no-brainer.

It's totally possible that this was part of the deal with Philly: If I sign for the minimum, commit to trading for Bronny and I'm in. So far, there's no indication that Bronny and LeBron is a package deal, but if LeBron's happiness was truly the North Star that brought him to Philly and he wants to continue playing with his son, the Sixers' business and basketball ops shouldn't think twice about doing LeBron a solid.

LeBron James has made $584 million in his NBA career. That's a bargain. Because of the max contract that artificially caps the earning power of the best players, James has effectively subsidized the contracts of the rest of his NBA peers while providing enormous surplus value for his squad.

In a 2024 study, a BYU economist Scott Kaplan showed that James' predicted salary in 2018-19 based on ticket sales, merchandise, popularity (as represented by All-Star votes) and player performance would be a whopping $123.3 million, nearly $100 million higher than his actual salary paid by the Lakers that season ($35.6 million). And that's just value to the Lakers. Kaplan asserted that due to James' ability to fill seats on the road, his value to the entire league was worth an annualized $229 million in salary.

Instead of James getting that money, it's distributed as part of the BRI (basketball-related income) to other players. Call it the LeBron James Subsidy. Nowadays, LeBron, at 41, doesn't spin up quite as much box-office magic as he did back then when he regularly led all players in All-Star votes.

Last season marked the first time in 22 years that he wasn't voted as a starter, but he still finished with the eighth-most votes in the league. By comparison, in 2018-19, Kevin Durant ranked eighth in All-Star votes and, according to Kaplan's model, provided $182 million in value to the NBA, with $98 million allocated directly to his team.

So what will LeBron be worth in 2026-27 as a Sixer? Let's throw in the fact that the cap has skyrocketed about 60% higher than it was in 2018-19. With revenues more frothy than at the time of Kaplan's study, we can roughly project James' predicted salary for his new team to be over $150 million and nearly $300 million in total value for the NBA. And that's pegging his value to a player ranking eighth in All-Star votes like KD in 2019.

So, yeah, James' economic value to his new team will dwarf his contract, and that was before he indicated that he was willing to play for the veteran's minimum of $3.9 million. Bronny's contract will pay him $2.3 million next season which is a rounding error compared to what James' on-court and off-court value will provide. Honestly, if Bronny's younger siblings Bryce and Zhuri were both old enough and entered the draft, teams would probably consider employing them too.

Bronny remains on the Lakers roster, but the team needs to trim at least one player in order to be in line with league roster rules. By going over the roster limit, Luka's team appears to be operating as if Bronny is expendable. Perhaps they truly believe he's the next GP2, the scrappy son of an NBA player that needed a few years to find his footing, and they find a way to keep him around. But they probably know he's worth more to LeBron's new team than his old one.

Both the Lakers and Sixers have some cap work to do. According to ESPN's Bobby Marks, Philadelphia is currently $572,000 above the first apron, so they have to shed salary. Dominick Barlow's $3.4 million for Bronny's $2.3 million would get them there. It might make more sense to find a home for Dalen Terry, who is already in a logjam in the backcourt before Bronny comes into the picture.

Maybe the Lakers play hardball with the Sixers and ask for a, um, King's ransom, but then again, no team drafted him early and made the Lakers sweat in 2024 despite everyone who paid one second of attention to draft coverage knowing the Lakers would seriously consider drafting Bronny at 55.

Is Bronny getting more opportunities because of his name? Probably. But he's the exception to the rule. Usually, sons of NBA players are snubbed rather than spoonfed. LeBron is the only one who stuck around long enough to make sure the second-generation snub didn't happen to his family. After all, Philadelphia is the City of Brotherly Love. LeBron and Bronny could make Fatherly Love a reality.

title: NBA superstar James, 41, to join Philadelphia 76ers
description: Basketball superstar LeBron James announces he will join the Philadelphia 76ers for what he says will be his final contract in the NBA.
fullText:
LeBron James has announced he will be joining the Philadelphia 76ers next season for what he says will be his final contract in the NBA.

The 41-year-old, the highest points scorer in the history of the league, left the Los Angeles Lakers after eight years last month.

The Cleveland Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors, Minnesota Timberwolves and Miami Heat were also rumoured to be in the running for the four-time NBA champion.

"I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energise a new fanbase and start this incredible journey one last time," James said on X., external

James has won an NBA title with all three teams he previously played for. He won two with Miami, who earlier this week mistakenly posted a link to an 'introductory press conference' for James.

A Heat spokesperson told Reuters, external the video was posted in error by staff who were preparing for the possibility of James rejoining the team he played for between 2010 and 2014.

Either side of that Miami stint, James had two spells with Cleveland, who drafted James in 2003 and are based near his hometown of Akron, Ohio.

"Miami I'll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always [be] home," James added.

James helped the Cavs become NBA champions in 2016 and joined the Lakers in 2018, claiming another NBA title two years later.

He has been named the NBA's Most Valuable Player four times, all between 2009 and 2013, and has been an NBA All-Star the last 22 seasons running.

James said after last season that he was "pretty sure I [had] played my last game" but realised "I still truly love this game and I have more to give".

ESPN has reported that James has signed a two-year contract, with a player option for the second year, worth $8m (£6m). His average salary with the Lakers last season was $50.7m (£38m).

James added: "I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point?

"I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship."

The 76ers reached the Conference semi-finals in last season's play-offs, where they lost to the eventual champions, the New York Knicks.

They have since acquired Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics, in exchange for Paul George and some future draft picks.

title: Biggest NBA offseason overreaction isn’t justified
description: NBA fan and media are overreacting far too much about this trade
fullText:
As NBA free agency dies down and the Summer League comes to an end, there’s less going on in the basketball world. Which means there’s going to be a lot more opinions and predictions. There have been countless blockbuster trades and signings this offseason, leaving people with plenty to talk about.

Undoubtedly, the biggest move of the offseason was Boston sending former Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia in exchange for Paul George and a couple of second-round picks. The majority of analysts and talking heads have already written the Celtics off, but is it a bit premature?

MORE: 3 NBA teams who are most improved entering 2026-2027 season

People are acting like Boston moving on from Jaylen Brown is the end-all, be-all. Boston did downgrade at the shooting guard position, slotting an aging Paul George into his place, but they also improved in other areas.

Their most significant upgrade came at center. It’s no secret that Boston has been searching for a reliable, physical center. They have brought in several players, but none could meet their expectations. They finally signed Knicks center Mitchell Robinson this offseason in hopes that he can solve that issue.

Robinson is an improvement over Nikola Vučević, and only time will tell how big of an impact this move will make.

Jaylen Brown is not a player you can easily replace, but how big of a downgrade is Paul George?

George is an above-average defender and a reliable scorer. He doesn’t measure up to Jaylen Brown, but in no way is he a bad basketball player. George averaged 17 points per game while shooting 40 percent from beyond the arc.

George provides a similar playstyle to Jaylen Brown while being less ball-dominant and a bit worse in nearly every area.

MORE: 3 NBA teams that have quietly won the offseason already

Boston made this trade to make it clear that Jayson Tatum is their guy. They essentially handed the keys to the offense to him, displaying full trust in their young superstar.

They improved at center and removed a ball-dominant player. The Celtics were able to finish second in the East without Tatum and with a lackluster center. With Tatum and a better center, who’s to say this team can’t finish first?

title: Shaquille O'Neal: LeBron James Ending Career With Cavaliers Would Be 'Historical'

fullText:
NBA legend Shaquille O'Neal believes LeBron James ending his career with the Cleveland Cavaliers would be "historical."

LeBron began his NBA career with the Cavaliers back in 2003. He played for the franchise from 2003-10 before going to the Miami Heat from 2010-14. The Akron native then returned to Cleveland from 2014-18 and helped delivered the team's first title in franchise history in 2016.

A future Hall of Famer, LeBron is currently a free agent for the first time since 2018. He's expected to sign with the Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors, Philadelphia 76ers or Minnesota Timberwolves.

Many people believe LeBron will sign with the Cavaliers. Cleveland assistant general manager Brandon Weems was with LeBron in Ohio a few weekends ago.

Weems is one of LeBron's closest friends.

"Let me talk to you about Brandon Weems," LeBron's agent, Rich Paul of Klutch Sports Group, said on his podcast. "Brandon Weems is basically LeBron's brother. Now, he worked his own way [up], nobody gave him anything. He's earned to be in the front office of the Cavs. But that is a big feather in the cap [for Cleveland], because of Brandon Weems."

It would certainly be cool to see LeBron end his career in Cleveland. A starting lineup of James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, LeBron, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen could compete for the championship next season.

The Cavaliers made the conference finals last season, losing to the New York Knicks in four quick games. Adding LeBron could make Cleveland title favorites next season.

If Harden signs for $30 million and if Cleveland can deal Max Strus and take back no salary in return, the Cavaliers would be able to give LeBron the mid-level exception.

For the Los Angeles Lakers last season, LeBron averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists per game. He's still an elite offensive player despite being the oldest active player in the NBA.

It will be interesting to see where LeBron is playing next season. Paul recently said on his podcast that LeBron will not be "rushed" into making a decision.

"We're not going to be rushed," Paul said on the latest podcast episode of "Game Over" with Max Kellerman and Rich Paul, released Monday evening. "We're not going to be rushed. It's his choice to make and when he makes the choice, he'll make it. ... I saw Adam in New York and we discussed it. And like I said, it's still his choice. So if he doesn't really know, you can't rush it. You can't rush it."

title: NBA Free Agency: More Jalen Duren Intel From Summer League
description: The Detroit Pistons are still working on a new deal for All-Star center Jalen Duren, but it is clear that a sign-and-trade will not be in store this summer
fullText:
Over the last several weeks, the basketball world has converged in Las Vegas for the Summer League. The Detroit Pistons had both of their draft picks in the lineup for each game, and essentially the whole team was there to support the Summer League squad even though they were only able to produce one victory (and four losses) in the series of exhibition games.

The word essentially was used in describing the Pistons’ team-wide support because 22-year old All-Star center Jalen Duren was notably absent from that contingent, but that is no surprise considering he’s still embroiled in contract negotiations with the club.

So far, there has not been an overwhelming amount of progress on either side. Duren would like a significant raise that is at least in the ballpark of a max contract, but the Pistons would feel more comfortable with a more team-friendly deal that allows for financial flexibility moving forward, which will be key since Ausar Thompson will be up next for a contract extension in due time.

In order to help understand that fluid situation, Spotrac’s Keith Smith spoke with multiple people within the Pistons organization, and he learned just where Detroit stands at the moment amid the important contract discussions being held with Duren and his representation.

“We very clearly want Jalen back with us for next year and beyond,” Smith’s front office source said. “If we didn’t, we could have easily done several different sign-and-trade deals. But the numbers have to be right. You saw what’s happened with Boston and OKC and New York. We don’t want to have to shed talent around Cade [Cunningham] and Jalen a year or two from now.”

Based on that statement, Pistons President of Basketball Operations Trajan Langdon is operating with the understanding that he will need to work out a contract extension with Thompson sooner rather than later, and he’d prefer not to handcuff Detroit before those discussions even begin. Right now, the Pistons have more than enough money to allocate for Duren’s upcoming deal, but they want to remain in a position to offer Thompson what he’s worth at the same time. But in any event, the Pistons have zero disillusions over the value that Duren adds to the team, so it is overwhelmingly likely that the two sides will come to an agreement in the near future.

“JD is a monster,” Smith was told by a Detroit assistant coach. “I don’t think any big man in the league has improved as much as JD has in his first four years in the league. Go look at his rookie year. He didn’t know what to do on defense, so he didn’t do much of anything. Last two years, he’s defending at a high level. He reads the floor well on offense. He’s super athletic. I hope everyone can be reasonable and we have him forever in Detroit.”

As a big man who averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds last season en route to an All-NBA Third Team selection, Duren is still adding to his skill set. That much was clear since Duren was a markedly improved shooter from the free throw line during the 2025-26 campaign, and he ended up finishing in second place for the Most Improved Player award as a result of his hard work.

Now, it’s the Pistons’ job to make sure that Duren continues working hard in the Motor City as opposed to any other location across the league.

title: LeBron’s Free Agency Continues to Stall NBA Offseason
description: James’s ongoing free agency has lasted longer than his previous three combined.
fullText:
LeBron James continues to hold up the rest of the NBA while he decides on his next team.

It has been 23 days since James parted ways with the Lakers after eight seasons, leading to nearly a month full of speculation as to where the 41-year-old will play next.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver recently said at a CNBC event last week that the league can’t formally set its schedule without knowing where one of its biggest stars will be playing.

“We have to finish up the schedule, and where LeBron plays affects the schedule,” Silver said. “It will influence how we set the schedule—opening week, Christmas. So I need him to make a decision.”

But James is also holding up the rest of free agency around the league as several key players remain unsigned, with the teams interested in them remaining in a holding pattern until the NBA’s all-time leading scorer makes up his mind.

A common denominator among some of the main unsigned free agents: They are also represented by Jame’s agent in Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul.

In most years, the NBA goes into hibernation in late July. The league’s personnel and media descend on Las Vegas for Summer League when most of free agency is wrapped up and then head out on vacation until the regular season comes within view in September.

But James is extending the offseason and is holding up deals for multiple teams and potential teammates as he ponders his destination.

“We’re definitely working later than usual,” one front office executive told Front Office Sports.

James’s free agency has extended longer than any of his previous ones combined. In 2010, he went eight days before announcing he would sign with the Heat during ‘The Decision.’ The time between his departure from Miami and return to Cleveland four years later lasted 10 days. And it took just 18 hours for James to announce he was heading west to Los Angeles in 2018 .

All of James’s free agencies began with an ending in mind. He ended his first one on ESPN, second with a Sports Illustrated op-ed, and third through the Klutch Sports X account. But the length of his current free agency leads one to wonder whether it has the gameplan his previous ones had.

First in line for new deals after James decides are James Harden (Cavaliers) and Draymond Green (Warriors). Harden declined his $42.3 million player option for next season on June 29, the day before James parted ways with the Lakers, to sign a long-term deal in Cleveland. Harden, who turns 37 next month, wants an NBA championship and is reportedly willing to sign for less money to have James alongside him.

The Cavaliers could potentially offer James the full mid-level exception of $15 million if Harden takes a pay cut and if the team trades Jarrett Allen and Max Strus. But if James is fine taking the veteran minimum of roughly $4 million, it wouldn’t be necessary.

Then there’s the case of Green, who declined his $27 million player option with the Warriors in an attempt to help lure James to Golden State. The Warriors can offer James the full mid-level exception without performing any trades, but it would require Green to sign for less. Green is another Klutch client James is keeping in limbo.

Peyton Watson, another Klutch client, and Jalen Duren, round out some of the other major un-signed free agents all awaiting a decision from James.

fullText:
Jul. 23—Obi Toppin has added drivers, irons and a putter to a bag of tricks that includes his signature between-the-legs EastBay dunk.

The former Dayton Flyers forward, now preparing for his seventh season in the NBA, held the Obi Open on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, at NCR Country Club. The event benefited the Toppin Family Foundation, which he founded earlier this month. Toppin's mom, Roni Toppin, is the president of the foundation.

The foundation's mission, according to its website, is to "create opportunity where it is needed most — supporting underprivileged children and families while investing in student-athletes who face financial hardship. We believe access to support, education, and athletics can change lives and strengthen our community for generations to come."

Toppin said they created the foundation to help the next generation. He had some struggles as a kid and wants to give kids a "better path to their dreams."

The golf outing was one of the foundation's first fundraising events. Toppin still shares many more basketball photos than golf photos on his Instagram profile, but the game is growing on him.

"My golf game is getting better every day," Toppin said. "It's all right. I can hold my own. I'm not the best golfer, but I'm getting better every single day."

Toppin, the consensus national player of the year in his final season at Dayton in 2020, wasn't the only former Dayton All-American on the course. DaRon Holmes II, who arrived at Dayton one year after Toppin departed, also played in the event.

"He told me it was his first time on a golf course," Toppin said. "I'm like, 'No way.' So I've got to get out there with him more and teach him golf."

Holmes signed autographs and posed for photos with members of the Flyer Faithful a day earlier at Lee's Famous Recipe Chicken in Kettering.

Obi Toppin: A tribute to a new Dayton Flyers hall of famer

Toppin returned to Dayton not only for the golf outing but for his sixth annual basketball camp. The Obi Toppin Basketball ProCamp, sponsored by CareSource, welcomed approximately 150 kids in grades one through eight to the University of Dayton RecPlex on Thursday. The camp continues Friday.

Toppin started the camp at the Bales Center in Beavercreek in 2021. In 2022, it moved to UD, where it has been held ever since.

"It's amazing," Toppin said. "I see a lot of familiar faces. I feel like it gets better and better every year, and it looks like there are more kids than previous years."

Toppin planned to head straight from the camp Thursday to speak to Dayton's current players at the Cronin Center. He met some of the players earlier in the week at a dinner.

Toppin could speak to the players about any number of experiences he's had in his career, including overcoming injuries. A foot injury marred his sixth NBA season and third with the Indiana Pacers. He played in the first three games of the season but didn't return to games until Feb. 26. He then appeared in 21 of the last 23 games.

One season after losing to the Oklahoma City Thunder in Game 7 of the NBA Finals, the Pacers finished with the second-worst record in the NBA and the worst record in franchise history (19-63). The team's star player, Tyrese Haliburton, missed the entire season after tearing his Achilles tendon in Game 7 last summer.

"There were a lot of injuries last year, but we have a healthier team this year," Toppin said. "We've got a great group of guys coming back, and I feel like our group has a really good chance."

The struggles of the Pacers coincided with the rise of Toppin's former team, the New York Knicks, who won the NBA championship one year after being eliminated by the Pacers in the Eastern Conference finals.

"I'm obviously close to the guys on that team, so I'm super happy for them," Toppin said. "They worked really hard to get to where they had to get to."

Now Toppin's goal is for the Pacers to follow the Knicks as champions.

"We've got to go get us one," Toppin said.
